steps.title: Go to the sign-in page yourself
steps.detail: Type the address of the service yourself, or use its app. Never use a link from an email or text that says your account is locked.
steps.why: Fake "account locked" messages are a common way to steal passwords.
steps.source_name: FTC: How to recognize and avoid phishing scams
steps.do_not: Do not give your password or a code to anyone who calls or writes to you.

steps.title: Microsoft account: follow the unlock steps
steps.detail: Sign in at account.microsoft.com. If it says the account is locked, follow the steps to get a security code by text and unlock it.
steps.why: Microsoft locks accounts when it sees unusual activity, to protect you.
steps.source_name: Microsoft: Microsoft account has been locked

steps.title: Microsoft: if that fails, use the recovery form
steps.detail: Use the sign-in helper first. If it does not work, fill in the account recovery form from a computer and place you often use.
steps.why: The form checks that you are the owner; a familiar device and place help.
steps.source_name: Microsoft: Help with the account recovery form

steps.title: Google account: use the account recovery page
steps.detail: Start from Google's account recovery page. Answer as many questions as you can, from a device and place you often use.
steps.why: Google checks the answers against what it knows about you.
steps.source_name: Google: Tips to complete account recovery steps

steps.title: Once you are back in, protect the account
steps.detail: Change the password to a new, long one and turn on two-step verification.
steps.why: An account that was locked may have been under attack.

steps.title: If you did not cause the lock, open the phishing plan
steps.detail: If you did not type a wrong password many times, someone else may have tried. Follow the phishing and stolen password plan.
steps.why: It is a sign that your password may be known.
steps.source_name: FTC: How to recognize and avoid phishing scams

steps.title: Still stuck? Call your IT contact
steps.detail: Tell them what you tried and what you see on screen. A photo of the screen helps.
steps.why: They can check settings and equipment you cannot reach.
